title: Brazilian policy weakens shark conservation | Science
content: In April, Brazil’s Ministries of Fisheries & Aquaculture and Environment enacted Interministerial Ordinance No. 30 authorizing targeted fishing of the blue shark (Prionace glauca) across national and international waters (1). Although presented as a sustainable fisheries measure, the ordinance substantially weakens shark conservation and contradicts Brazil’s international commitments under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) (2). The Brazilian government should reevaluate this ordinance through a transparent, science-based process and expedite shark conservation measures.
